question: If the selling price is ₹2,886 after allowing a discount of 26% on the marked price, then the amount of discount is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Marked Price (MP) be 100%.

Selling Price % = 100% − 26% = 74%.

Here, 74% corresponds to ₹2,886.

Amount of discount (26%) = (2886 ÷ 74) × 26

⇒ 39 × 26 = ₹1,014

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,014.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 ? = ₹1,014

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP) = ₹2,886

Discount = 26%

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

Discount amount = MP − SP

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2886 = MP × (100 − 26) ÷ 100

⇒ 2886 = MP × (74 ÷ 100)

⇒ MP = (2886 × 100) ÷ 74

⇒ MP = 39 × 100 = ₹3,900

⇒ Discount amount = 3900 − 2886

⇒ Discount amount = ₹1,014

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,014.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price printed on an article or the label price. A discount is always calculated on the marked price.

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, then the effective single discount is: a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100.

Markup Percentage

It is the percentage by which the marked price is higher than the cost price. Markup % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.
